summary.text: 女 is a whole-figure pictograph of a woman, now meaning “woman; female.” Early forms are interpreted as a kneeling or seated figure, with accounts differing on the hands’ position.

formation.text: Pictographic: the whole graph depicts a woman. Early forms are interpreted as a kneeling figure with hands crossed at the chest; some forms are described with an added head stroke interpreted as headwear.

components.text: The whole graph depicts a woman; early forms are interpreted as a kneeling figure, sometimes with a head stroke interpreted as headwear. It is not divided into smaller parts.

history.text: Oracle-bone forms are described as a kneeling woman with hands crossed before the chest; some add a head stroke interpreted as headwear. The kneeling posture becomes less apparent in Spring and Autumn bronze forms, and Warring States forms continue those forms with changed stroke manner. Clerical writing turns the vertical kneeling stroke into a horizontal stroke.

Early accounts report 女 used for 母 in an oracle-bone example, for 汝 in bronze inscriptions, and for 如 in Warring States writing. These reported readings are distinct from changes in the graph’s written form; the available evidence does not establish a dated sequence among these uses.

uncertainties.text: Descriptions differ in details of early forms. One source describes crossed hands and sometimes a head stroke interpreted as headwear; other accounts describe a seated or kneeling figure and differ on the hands. The proposed modern-form reversal and breast interpretation are not confirmed by the inspected paleographic accounts.
Early inscription accounts report uses of 女 beyond “woman,” but the available dates and contexts do not establish whether each is a borrowed spelling for another word or a development in meaning.

senses.text: Early inscription accounts report female-related uses; a later dictionary glosses 女 as “woman.” The cited inscription examples are not precisely dated here, so they document early use without proving the graph’s original meaning or priority among early uses. The ordinary meaning “woman; female” is current.
Early inscription accounts report 女 used for 母, including cited oracle-bone examples. This documents an early use or overlap, but does not establish a semantic development from “woman.”

senses.text: Inscription accounts report 女 used for 毋, 每/悔, 汝, 如, and place names. The evidence does not establish whether these were borrowed spellings for other words or meanings of 女, and it gives no dated sequence among them.

A separate lexical reading is recorded with the meaning “give as a wife.” The supplied historical readings distinguish it from 女 “female,” but do not date this use or establish how the meanings are related.

Present-day definition records list “girl” and “feminine”; a dictionary also lists daughter or unmarried girl. These listed meanings do not establish when they arose or how they developed from “woman.”

limitations.text: The reported uses and dictionary glosses do not establish dated transitions among these meanings, so no semantic-development links are asserted.
